Although many such problems feature global optimums, their solution often demands extensive computational resources. Consequently, a prevalent approach employs numerous underperforming approximations, termed evolution strategies (ES), which sample and refine high-quality candidates. A critical insight for ES is maximizing information utilization from each evaluation point. Recently, adaptive approximation models have emerged to enhance the accuracy of likelihood functions for ES by improving how evaluation data is leveraged. In this work, we introduce a novel architecture, a conditional random function (CRF), designed as a robust tool for ES. We evaluate this network within two specific model classes: univariate and bivariate ES. Initially, we assess its efficacy as a local surrogate model. Subsequently, we examine its utility in a global context through a hybrid optimization framework combining it with random restarts. Experimental results demonstrate that this surrogating ES outperforms current adaptive methods in univariate cases and matches the performance of state-of-the-art surrogating ES in bivariate scenarios. Finally, we propose directions for future research.

numerous deep learning models have emerged in both research and industry settings. To address this, the study introduces a new radiative transfer simulation approach designed to model apparent structural changes in zones like the CMZ. Results indicate simulating internal variability successfully accounts for observed discrepancies in cloud separation distances, sizes, and brightness. Therefore, using simple homogeneous cloud models should be avoided when interpreting distance estimates or morphological features in cold, dense galactic central zones.

We introduce the concept of the co-q-function for the stiffer quasin-static regime, developing theoretical tools to analyze expandin g quark-gluon plasma. Applying the revised framework, we perform a co-q statistical analysis of hadron species observed in central LHC collisions and determine the corresponding q values for various hadron types. The results reveal that q varies significantly based hadronic mass and chemical freeze-out temperature, with the co-q approach yielding better statistical agreement for the q-parameter than the traditional model. Furthermore, we compute the co-q entropy and find that, unlike the standard model, it decreases as hadronic multiplicities rise. Finally, by examining the q-value trends across different hadronic distributions, the study offers fresh insights into the formation and evolution of the expanding quark-gluon plasma.

In this study, we introduce and validate a novel two-dimensional (2D) numerically accurate (NA) magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) reconnecting current sheet (RCS) for high-fidelity analysis. Employing this tool, we conduct a rigorous, parameterized investigation of collisionless fusionetic magnetic reconnection using both global NA MHD and locally linear stability (LTS) analyses. Our results demonstrate excellent agreement between predictions from RCS and LTS, with reconnection rates in RCS enhanced by approximately an order of magnitude. We identify that local linear theory accurately forecasts the aspect ratio of 0.5 for optimal efficiency and finds that increasing ion-diffusion coefficients always broadens the RCS, yet only elevates the rate if it simultaneously reduces ion temperature. Furthermore, findings confirm that the configuration with fastest fusion is magnetic field strength symmetric, in contrast to previous studies suggesting strength-based asymmetry. Finally, we establish that the configuration is robust, surviving in 50% of all instances, and demonstrate that the resulting rate is consistent across different models.
